speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and are they constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms fluctuating with activity and improving with rest strongly suggest a neuromuscular issue; do you experience any drooping eyelids or difficulty speaking clearly during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with double vision triggered by looking up or down, is highly suggestive of a myasthenic crisis or Myasthenia Gravis. Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing food or liquids, or any choking episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies AND MuSK_Antibodies. REQUEST IMAGES: Eye_Examination_for_ptosis_and_ophthalmoplegia. Have you noticed any improvement in your symptoms after taking any specific medication, particularly if it contains anticholinesterase agents?
